question.leadin: This period succeeded the Tokugawa Shogunate.
question.text: Name this period of rapid industrialization and modernization under a namesake emperor from 1869 to 1912 in Japan. The goals of the Emperor, restored to full power, were outlined in the Charter Oath.
question.clue: In addition to the creation of the Charter Oath, this event also saw the passage of a constitution modeled on Prussia's.

swap.leadin: This emperor gave the "Jewel Voice Broadcast" to announce his country's surrender in World War II.
swap.text: Name this emperor of an Asian country that fought against the US in the Pacific Theatre of World War II.
swap.clue: This regent led a country during the Mukden Incident, which served as a pretext for his nation's invasion of Manchuria.

question.leadin: Its founder was one of the three great unifiers of a certain country, along with Oda Nobunaga and Toyotomi Hideyoshi.
question.text: Name this shogunate, which was established after the Battle of Sekigahara and ruled from 1603 to 1868.
question.clue: This clan adopted sakoku until the arrival of the "black ships" of Matthew Perry.

swap.leadin: The busiest one of these locations in the United States is Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International.
swap.text: Name these locations, such as O'Hare International. These locations often require extensive security checks before a traveller is allowed near a runway.
swap.clue: After several Montoneros and Peronists gathered at one of these places, right-wing snipers shot into the crowd during the Ezeiza massacre.

question.text: After the Battle of Dan-no-ura, Minnamoto no Yoritomo became the first Kamakura ruler to possess this title. People from the Tokugawa family held this title used to refer to military dictators of Japan.
question.clue: A power vacuum created after the death of a holder of this title led to the Onin War, which initiated the Sengoku period.

swap.text: Before Tokugawa and Toyotomi, this victor at Okehazama was the first of Japan's unifiers, helping end the Warring-States period. He committed suicide at Honno-ji temple in Kyoto.
swap.clue: This man's troops used matchlocks to repulse the charge of Takeda cavalry at the Battle of Nagashino.

question.leadin: Answer the following about the life of Julia Ota, a young prisoner of war from 16th century Korea.
question.text: Julia was adopted by Konishi Yukinaga, a leading general during this leader's late-1500s invasion of Korea.
question.clue: This leader, who initiated construction of Osaka Castle, led failed invasions of Korea in 1592 and 1598.

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about the Hojo clan.
swap.text: The Hojo were the effective rulers during this shogunate named for a city that's today famous for a large Buddha statue. This shogunate took power after the Heian period.
swap.clue: Its puppet rulers attempted to revolt with the Jokyu war, but were crushed and remained silent for another century.

question.text: Classified into Nozomi, Hikari, and Kodama categories, these help commuters travel around Honshu.

swap.text: Aso created controversy when he was caught lying about comments he had made opposing Hiromu Nonaka's bid for Prime Minister on the grounds that Nonaka belonged to this ethnic group, subject to discrimination in Japan over their descent from certain "outcast" communities.
swap.clue: This still-shunned Japanese minority inherits its reduced social standing from people outside the Tokugawa caste system, who lived in separate hamlets where they performed ritually-unclean jobs such as butchery.

question.text: After Japan's defeat in World War II, Hirohito managed to avoid the war crimes trials that condemned this Prime Minister. This man survived a 1945 suicide attempt before his execution by hanging in 1946.
question.clue: This leader of the Chahar Expeditionary Force ordered troops to attack Hebei Province following the Marco Polo incident.

swap.leadin: This work's title character marries Lady Aoi before fathering his only child with Akashi's daughter.
swap.text: Name this Heian period work, sometimes called the world's first novel, written by Lady Murasaki.
swap.clue: This work, often called the world's first novel, is an important insight into Heian court life. It features the blank chapter "Vanished into the Clouds" and was written by Lady Murasaki Shikibu.

question.leadin: During one of these events, soldiers fought on and around large walls at Iki-no-matsubara, and before these events a letter was sent addressed to the "ruler of a small country."
question.text: Name these events chronicled by Suenaga, the second of which was repelled by a fleet-crushing "divine wind."
question.answerHtml: Mongol invasions of Japan [or Yuan invasions of Japan; or Kublai Khan’s invasions of Japan; accept equivalents for invasion like “attack”; prompt on “Chinese invasion of Japan”; prompt on “invasions of Japan”]
question.clue: During one of these conflicts, an exaggerated 142,000-strong army was defeated at the battle of Hakata Bay.

swap.text: In correspondence with Emperor Yang of Sui, this prince encouraged him to call Japan by Nihon. Through the Seventeen-Article Constitution, he promoted Buddhism as Japan's state religion.

question.leadin: The period named for this city saw the introduction of the Yoro law code and lasted until Emperor Kammu ordered the relocation of the capital to Nagaoka.
question.text: Name this city, laid out on a grid to resemble Chang'an, that served as capital of Japan from 710 to 784.
question.clue: This was the first time when emperors adopted the title of "tenno," and other innovations during this period, such as the institution of a Council of State, were adopted in order to imitate the government at Changan and important Tang Chinese institutions.

swap.leadin: This family rose to power by defending Emperor Go-Shirakawa in the Hogen and Heiji Wars, then imprisoned Go-Shirakawa to rule during the Rokuhara Regime.
swap.text: Name this Japanese clan whose defeat at the Battle of Dan-no-Ura sealed their loss of the Gempei War to the Minamoto.
swap.clue: This clan is referenced in an incipit ("in-SIP-it") that evokes the "sound of the Gion Shoja bells."

question.leadin: Answer some questions about the Genpei War.
question.text: The war concluded with this naval battle won by Yoshitsune off Honshu's southern coast, in Shimonoseki Strait. After it, Yoshitsune's older brother, Minamoto Yuritomo, established the Kamakura shogunate.
question.clue: This battle saw Taguchi Shigeyoshi reveal the location of the Emperor's ship, and both the child-emperor Antoku and his grandmother, the widow of Kiyomori, committed suicide.

swap.text: The end of Hojo power came when this warlord overthrew Hojo Takatoki and established himself as shogun in 1336, thus beginning the Muromachi period, which was also known by his clan's name.

question.leadin: Answer the following about ancient legal codes.
question.text: This 645 CE set of policies promulgated in Japan shortly after the death of Prince Shotoku established the Ritsuryo, a strange mix of Legalistic laws and Confucian rhetoric adapted for Japanese conditions.
question.clue: This set of laws promulgated during the Asuka period, which curtailed the power of regional governors and imported traditions like the equal field system from China.

swap.leadin: One of these structures is named after the Japanese word for chopsticks, Hashihaka, due to its resemblance to those utensils, and is thought to contain the body of the mythical queen Pimiko.
swap.text: Name these keyhole-shaped megalithic tombs in Japan. The era lasting from roughly the 3rd century to the 6th century is named for them.
swap.clue: A scholarly debate centers on whether two objects with raised left arms found in one of these places depict horse herders or dancers.
